### Round one: four checks in parallel on a frozen copy (screen, game, code, and accuracy with the lessons)

- The four read a frozen copy of the pass as built, with a packet of the changes, Mikey's message, every welcome's words and screenshots; each report is kept word for word in the pass's working folder (r1), which the checkpoint zips carry.
- The facts (the accuracy and lesson check, against published sources): four welcome lines repeated errors that had sat in the games' written help since they were built, and the welcome now said them aloud. Read the Jar called a soil of 70 percent sand or more sandy, but by the USDA's texture classes (the NRCS Soil Survey Manual, 2017, as ISRIC's flow chart tabulates it) 70 percent sand with 10 percent clay is a sandy loam, and 1,526 of the game's 4,000 sandy jars were; sandy now begins at 85 percent (jarTexture and jarRounds), every jar the game draws lands in the USDA class its answer names, and Soil and plants (agriculture 9 to 12) teaches the rule before the game ("A soil of eighty-five percent sand or more, with little clay, is sandy, one of forty percent clay or more is a clay, and most mixes in between are loams."). Pay the Price said "a dot for every coin" while a big coin fills five dots; it says "A small coin fills one dot, and a big coin fills five.", and kindergarten economics, which never teaches a coin worth five, is earmarked for it (EARMARKS A47). Ask the Right Question said "A question about you wobbles", where only 4 of its 24 wrong questions are about the asker; "A question about something else wobbles." Teach the Robot said each lesson changes "every guess", where one changes 1 to 6 of the 12; "watch the guesses near it change". Hold It in Mind claimed to "stretch your working memory", a benefit training has not been shown to give beyond similar tasks (Melby-Lervåg, Redick and Hulme, 2016); "This game shows you how much your working memory can hold." The made o's resonances followed neither cited study; its comment now says they sit between the two.
- Taken from its considerations: Mean, Median, Mode had the repeated score in the middle of every one of its 18,000 rounds, so the median was always the mode and the welcome's two rules never gave different answers; the repeated score now sits low or high, and the rules test holds the three averages apart. Balance the scale names what its left pan shows by deck (a number, a times fact, a fraction, an expression to work out); Pong is "a quick break for your eyes and your hands" and counts "hits in a row"; Cut the Fillers "helps you catch filler words"; Sort the Because's fakes include an order, as its lesson says; Grow the Plant says "Listen to what the plant looks like."; the mode is "the score that appears most", the lesson's words; the early-years story direction is shorter, [calm and unhurried, a voice for each character], since every early clip carries it; and the voice check page names short i by igloo, as the lessons do. Owls' ear tufts are feathers (their ears are openings on either side of the head, about level with the eyes, as Illinois Wildlife's "Owl ears" puts it), so Match the land animals, which shows the owl just after its ears lines, now says "The tufts on top of its head are feathers, not ears.", and the delivery tells Mikey.
- Declined from its considerations: Name the Feeling's "Look at the eyebrows, the eyes and the mouth." stays, as the game's guidance on where to look rather than a fact it asks; and the silent-e story's "the a says aa" waits with the bare vowels for Mikey's answer to Q60 (EARMARKS A42).
- All three of the screen, game and code checks found the same two faults first. Ending a welcome while its pointer had the game's question said (Skip, Close, the round arrow, Instructions or the speaker, in Which Sense, Spot It, Find the Letter, Share the Cookies, Grow the Plant or Find the Tool) left every voice in the app silent until a reload: the ask gave the welcome's hush back after the welcome had ended. And the boards that say their question as they open (Which Sense, Share the Cookies, Spot It, Grow the Plant, Find the Letter) said it before the welcome hushed them, so a child heard half a question cut off. The hush is now taken in a layout effect, which React runs before any board's effects, and held once, so nothing can give it back after the welcome has gone; the browser test plays Skip, Close and the round arrow during an ask and hears the game's question afterwards, reads that the first words said are the welcome's, and counts the question only while the pointer asks it (the old count had passed on the leaked question, and passed with the ask's press planted out).
- The code check found that a pace change during this pass's new pauses (the snail's breath between sentences, the gap after a title or a paragraph, the fifth of a second between two sounds) said a sentence again ("Ana had a plate.", "Two Plates."). The reader's place now moves on before a pause begins (onRest in sayPieces, the next text in speakSequence's gap), and the snail's breath now falls beside a sound too ("Bus." and sss had come 5 ms apart); the rules test runs a pace change, a stop and a lost end in each pause, each case failing on the code before the fix.
- The code and game checks found that the round every welcome played, 977, was one more than a multiple of 4, 8, 16 and 61, so in fourteen games the pointer solved the child's own first set (Debug the robot showed the very program the child then had to fix), and the game check counted 47 games whose welcome answered one of the child's first three items. Each game now takes its own round (demoRoundFor in logic.mjs): from 500 up, the first whose answered items the child never meets in round 1, else the one whose items the child meets latest; the boards deal through logic's own functions (dealIndex, mixOrder, mapOrder, jumpQuestions, balanceTargets, searchBoardAt and the round generators), which the scripts test holds them to, so the rules test reads what the boards deal. Only the two smallest decks (Spot It's four pictures and In order: civilizations' three sets) cannot keep clear of the first three, and take the round whose items the child meets latest (round two found Buckets and Pairs still outside this, below); the check fails on 977 (fifty games) and on round 1 (every game with a run of items).

Since the checks: tests/scripts.test.mjs reads every drawn picture on every line, the ones that open with an instruction word too; tests/stories.test.mjs holds a [pause] and a voice in every early story from S3931 on; the rules test reads the young voice's rests on both sides, Find the Letter's backstop (voiceBackstopMs) and the outline by fill; tests/e2e/game-intro.mjs reads the six spoken rows on a 320 phone and one held sideways, the answer boxes through whole rounds, Find the Tool's tiles on every board, and a welcome line whose voice never reports its end; tests/e2e/question-screens.mjs presses a lesson's Say it again; tests/e2e/click-through.mjs carries the store across a reload whole and goes on after a failed refresh.
- tools/voice-check.mjs: the rows regrouped for Q60, the young voice in its plays, its self-test. tools/audio-ledger.mjs: [pause] between a welcome's sentences; the young closing line and the six Q66 lines as clips of their own.

- The lesson and accuracy check (all 26 kinds over 2,000 seeds, each word of every question, reason and explanation read against the spoken script alone) found nine things to fix and ten to consider, all taken: Tap the picture for an event offered a picture a child could fairly tap (the book for bedtime, the bed for story time, the book for a birthday party, on 27, 19 and 29 of seeds 1 to 400), so those pictures are never offered there (PE_TAP_NOT, held by the rules test's own list); "Which one is a person?" was asked and the script said only "people", so the lesson says "Each one is a person."; glad's question always showed the sad face, and every face reason used a sign the course never says, so glad's wrong faces are the mad and scared ones and the lesson says each sign ("Glad means happy, with a big smile. Angry means mad, with eyebrows that squeeze down. Afraid means scared, with wide-open eyes."); the coat icon was a short-sleeved shirt (now long sleeves, also for civics-k's thick coat and science-1's warm coat); "I want a cup of juice. is not about what your friend said." was heard as a sentence and a fragment, so a wrong reply is named "Saying, I want a glass of water" and every wrong command by doing it ("Talking at the same time would mean ..."); four yes-or-no reasons did not fit their questions ("Yes would mean they do, but they do not." after "Are glad and happy opposites?"), so each row has its own (held by a new rules check that a reason names a word of its question); "right in your friend's face" was never shown as too close, and now is said; four older citations still said taking turns in conversations waits or an expressive half waits (Please and thank you, Can I play too?, Big and little, Colours), now brought up to date, and Words that go together's II.D.1 citation names what Helpers all around teaches; the earmarks read against the citations (E12, E13 and the map). ### What was built

- **Q71 (a, his rule kept): a phone held sideways asks to be turned upright, and stays asking.** The rules for the ask had sat inside a stray pair of braces, which browsers drop with everything in them, so the ask had never shown since the day the braces went in ("I was wondering why it stopped one day"). The rules stand on their own now, and the ask draws a phone turning upright (still with less motion), on every screen of the app on a phone turned on its side; tablets and laptops never see it. tests/site.test.mjs reads the rule from the page and four screens sideways, proven failing on pass MQ's page.
- **Q72: Grow the Plant.** The hint keeps its room above the tiles from the start, so a wrong tap's red-brown words appear in place and nothing moves ("I like the location above the tiles and think that holding a place for it is a good idea"); after a right answer the praise is said to its end, then a beat of a second (NEXT_QUESTION_BEAT_MS), and the next question never comes sooner than 2.2 seconds after the tap (RIGHT_ANSWER_HOLD_MS, afterSaid in src/ui.jsx); each tile's word is fitted to its tile (FitText), so "sunshine" stays inside its button; and the Walkthrough Mode tab hangs from the top of the green frame, centered, where it covers nothing (at the bottom left it sat over the game's Instructions link in his screenshot); tests/e2e/scroll-cue.mjs reads it clear.
- **Centered words never pushed by a speaker, app-wide ("I never want this to happen anywhere in the app and try to correct every example I find").** SpokenRow, the row that sets a speaker beside centered words, keeps a column of at least 44 pixels on each side, so the words center on the board whatever the speaker's width; then every game was swept for the two faults he named. tests/e2e/layout-check.mjs finds a word that spills out of its box and centered words that sit off center; tools/layout-sweep.mjs opens every game (160) at eight sizes, in a normal and a tenth-wider font, and after a wrong tap; check.sh step 13g runs the narrowest phone, the wide font and the wrong tap. Fixed on the way: the game head rows wrap on narrow phones, Mean/Median's scores wrap, the periodic table game's symbols fit their cells (min(15px, 3.9vw)), and Who Gains' words fit their tiles.
- **The closing line (Q68 c, with his words).** Every game's spoken welcome closes "But most importantly, HAVE FUN!!!": from grade 3 up "If you wish to hear these instructions again, simply tap the speaker near the bottom of the page. But most importantly, HAVE FUN!!!" and in all 35 young games "To hear this again, tap the speaker at the bottom. But most importantly, HAVE FUN!!!" (GAME_INTRO_CLOSING and GAME_INTRO_CLOSING_YOUNG), the capitals said as a cheer (CHEER_RUN and cheerTagged in src/logic.mjs, the cheer shape on the device voice and [excited] for the recorded one).
- **Q69 (c): red-brown on a game's piece means a wrong answer.** In 36 games the pieces that were red-brown for their own reasons take an edge of their own (edu-own-edge), Better Deal's coupons are blue and violet, the Valid, Reason and flag buttons have neutral ink edges (the flag's red swatch #D33A3A), the struck filler word is gray (#6B7068), and Split the Search's part above the line is lavender (#E3D7F5). Left as (c) said in its own words: the red-brown name a swipe card shows while it is dragged left in seven games, and five boards' red-brown lines, bars and rings (Build the Fund, Break Even, Fill the Jar, Shape the Sound, Push to the Beat); outside the games red-brown still marks what needs practice (round three's alignment read: the rule had been written wider than (c), "nothing else", so a later check would have changed what Mikey kept).
- **Q67 (b, made fun): say the new word with me.** Eight young vocabulary lessons, Mikey's four (Learning words, Words for people, More learning words and Words that go together) and the four halves Q70 split from them, end a line with a cue that names the new word and then says it in a silly voice for the child to say along: a tiny whisper, nice and slow, four times in a low, silly voice, three times super fast, stretched out long, a squeaky little voice, or a happy cheer (SAY_WITH_ME in src/logic.mjs, each with its device-voice shape and its recorded voice's tag), no lesson using one voice twice in a row. 31 cues in all. Nothing is recorded or heard by the app; read-aloud stays output only. Each of these lessons shows the note that the spoken audio is not final in a panel under its buttons ("This page will be very important to mark with our not final audio message"). tests/scripts.test.mjs holds every cue to its word said just after it, the cue to the end of its line and each lesson to a new voice each time, with six near misses.
- **Q70 (c): the nine long pre-K lessons are eighteen whole lessons.** Each was split where its ideas part ("If more educational value or high quality explanatory context comes from extra length, I would always choose the extra length", so no half was cut for length): pre-K 3's Talking with a friend and Talk about it; Two steps and Two steps every day; Two ideas and Who has what; Learning words and Count and sort; People and events, now Words for people, and Things that happen; pre-K 4's Let's play together and Play with a plan; Three steps and Three steps every day; More learning words and Rhymes and shapes; Words that go together and Same and opposite. Each half has its own spoken script, its own story (new stories S3951 to S3986 where a half had none), its own coloring page (D255 to D263), five or more question kinds with their re-derivations in PREK_DERIVE, citations split with "in part" naming what the other half teaches, and its requires repointed (checkPrerequisiteGraph clean). Talk about it's why bank grew from one question to five; three long morals were shortened to the read-aloud guideline; the direction words every half's questions use (first, second, last) are said in its own script, which tests/scripts.test.mjs reads for the six direction lessons. review-status.json marks the nine new and nine shortened lessons. A long lesson is Q70 (c)'s own measure, 14 lines or more, and two halves reached it through the checks' fixes, each added line drawing a picture its questions show (Who has what, 12 to 14 lines in round one; Rhymes and shapes, 12 to 14 in round two), so both stay whole by Mikey's words (round three's alignment read).
- **The 2027 pre-K recommendations, adopted.** The committee's recommended revisions of the 2022 Texas Prekindergarten Guidelines were read from Mikey's five PDFs character by character, by each character's color and its strike or underline bar, and checked against every page rendered as an image: docs/standards/tea-pk3-2027-recommended.txt (123 outcomes) and tea-pk4-2027-recommended.txt (132), whose notes list every slip the committee's editing left and how it is read. Two independent checks with code of their own read every outcome again (no wrong word, code, missing or extra outcome; their notes folded in, the less certain reading of PK4 VI.D.2 named in EARMARKS). Then all 69 pre-K lesson citations were requoted to the 2027 outcome, naming "Texas Prekindergarten Guidelines (2027 recommendations)"; renumbered outcomes follow their new numbers (the committee moves Mathematics' Geometry, Measurement and Classification from C, D and E to B, C and D, Science's Physical, Life and Earth from A, B and C to B, C and D beside a new A and E, and some counting outcomes within V.A); the four outcomes the lessons cited that the committee deleted are cited no more (pre-K 3's II.B.4, folded into II.B.1 and II.B.2, so Please and thank you cites II.B.2 in part; II.D.2, whose place the old II.D.3 takes as instructional and academic vocabulary; II.E.4, so Two ideas and Who has what cite II.A.1 in part; and V.C.4, folded into V.B.1), and pre-K 4's 2022 VI.A.2, position and motion, became VI.B.2, push, pull and collision, which Match the solids does not teach, so it now waits in docs/EARMARKS.md. The four pre-K plans in src/curriculum.mjs have 2027 codes and words, rows for deleted outcomes gone, and new rows for 2027 outcomes the lessons now teach (pre-K 3's VI.B.1, III.B.5, VI.D.2, VI.C.1, VII.B.3 and VII.A.3, pre-K 4's VII.A.3). tests/coverage.test.mjs holds each quote to the file of the edition its citation names and fails a pre-K lesson that quotes a Texas outcome without naming 2027, with a 2027 near miss. docs/EARMARKS.md has the 2027 domain map (what waits, domain by domain) and docs/standards/README.md the edition rule. TEA had not adopted the recommendations when they were read; when it does, the adopted text is read against these files.
- **People that look more like people (placeholders until the paintings).** The doctor, baby, teacher, grandma and grandpa icons were redrawn with real proportions, faces with eyes that catch the light, brows, hair with shape, and clothes (IconPic); Whose Turn Next's four friends and the face game's face are one new kid drawing (KidFace: four looks in KID_LOOKS, with shoulders, shaded skin, eyes that catch the light, brows and hair with shape, and the feelings face KID_FEELING_FACE, whose eyes, brows and mouth make each feeling the game asks, scared a tense grimace, never a laugh), each friend clipped to its seat with ids from useId. The four Wonder voices' stand-in portraits stay flat, as Mikey chose for their paintings in Q33; Q73 asks whether they should follow the new style.

Smith, Here We Are by Oliver Jeffers, Just Because by Mac Barnett, I Wonder by Annaka Harris and Q is for Question by Tiffany Poirier; his screenshot showed Just Because and I Wonder by title and price alone, so the editions that fit a list about wonder were chosen, and he is told so: Rebecca Elliott's Just Because and Kari Anne Holt and Kenard Pak's I Wonder share the titles) and 22 more books about wonder or long recommended by teachers, each on the list of the age it suits (among them Owl Moon, They All Saw a Cat, Last Stop on Market Street, The Most Magnificent Thing, Me...Jane, Beautiful Oops!, The Three Questions, Wonder Walkers, Snowflake Bentley, The Dot, Dark Emperor and Other Poems of the Night, Starry Messenger, Grand Canyon, Your Place in the Universe, Mistakes That Worked, The Invention of Hugo Cabret, The Evolution of Calpurnia Tate, The Little Prince, The Girl Who Drew Butterflies, Sophie's World, A Short History of Nearly Everything 2.0 and The Sense of Wonder): 281 books on 17 lists. Fly Guy, The Lion & the Mouse, Adventures of Huckleberry Finn), authors and retellers named (Ox-Cart Man by Donald Hall with Barbara Cooney, Cinderella by Charles Perrault with Kinuko Y. A read of every question picture (110 banks in the real app on a phone) and every lesson picture (860 pictures of 78 kinds, drawn by the app's own components) found words past the picture's edge, words on top of each other, lines through words and words too faint, and every one was fixed: the coordinate grid's x-axis numbers (drawn below the picture's edge since they were written, so no reader ever saw them) and its point's label, which was the answer to the question beside it, hidden on that question; the percent grid's and the beaker's captions; the cell, its parts now named outside it on thin leader lines, where "chloroplast" had sat beside no chloroplast at all; timelines whose last years ran off the right edge ("1991, the Web", "1836, San Jacinto"), now spread inside the picture along each side of the line (spreadLabels); five growing bars whose fifth ran off the edge; a reaction's third product; the functions lesson's point (3, 7), drawn above the picture's top with its label, so the picture never showed the point its caption names; map names past the edge and on coastlines, now inside with a thin white outline; an open number line's names stacked in two touching rows, now one row with short leaders; the forces caption; "evaporation" on its own arrow; "equilibrium" on the supply line; "sin" on the unit circle; the end-behavior and shift words on their curves; a wave's "amplitude" on the wave; the Earth's layers, now named on leader lines ("crust" had sat on its own outline, and the inner core was "inner" to fit); the branches' arrow through "carries out"; a sign whose white words ran off it ("cabin to candle"); stacks and two-way boxes whose words had shrunk past reading; the mixture's two captions running together; the pyramid's caption on its bottom level; "night" written white on the white page; the triangle's and the parallelogram's "height" crossed by a slanted side; a 20 degree angle's number on its own side, now on each angle's bisector; and a number line's "-10-9-8". Some drawings were corrected on the way: a wave's wavelength bar spans exactly one wavelength, crest to crest (it had been 40 units whatever the wave), with its amplitude drawn at a crest; sliding plates move along their boundary, one up and one down, as at a transform boundary; powers are written 2³, not 2^3; and every arrow and the periodic table are drawn in the paper palette, since in the dark theme the periodic table's symbols had been the live palette's cream on pastel cells, unreadable. tests/e2e/diagram-words.mjs (check.sh step 13h; run with tsx) reads every one of these pictures in both themes for all four faults, a word read a twelfth wider than the test machine draws it, since a phone's font runs wider; proven failing on the drawings before the fixes.

### The checks

- **Round one: twelve checks in parallel on a frozen copy (frozen-mr-r1, 01:30 on October 28).** The lesson check and the accuracy check of the eighteen halves (every kind run over 2,000 and 20,000 seeds and re-derived with tables of their own), the story check and the story flow check, the standards read of the 2027 adoption (all 69 pre-K modules, 134 citations), four book checks (281 entries, every book against at least one fetched source; the shared web search allowance ran out near the end), the picture check (the ledger's 45 new rows and the drawings), the screen check and the code check. What they found, and what changed:
  - **The split lessons (lesson check, 14 to fix).** Talk about it asked "How may your friend feel?" with a sad face this half never drew (now drawn beside the pizza), and its words "feel you did not listen" became "think you did not listen". The two "every day" halves used numbered tapping in most of their kinds but only the first halves said how it works, so a child arriving weeks later was never told (each now says it on its own colored circles or shapes). Learning words asked about red and blue triangles it never drew (its match kind keeps to the circle and square), Words for people asked "Which one is a person?" against a cake, a bed, a book and a slide whose reasons were Things that happen's (a new line, "A book, a bed and a cake are not people. They are things."), and cited VII.B.3's family helpers though no line said a grandma or grandpa helps (now each "can help take care of you", and "A teacher, a doctor, a grandma and a grandpa are all helpers."). Let's play together asked one face question in every round, its wrong faces never drawn (a line now draws all four, and four questions take turns, one a mad face a grab can bring). Play with a plan offered a tower it never drew and asked what a friend "might say" with "No, never!" as a fair answer (now "What is a kind thing your friend might say?"). Count and sort and Rhymes and shapes told a wrong tap "Three dots is how many a triangle has." (now "Three dots are as many as the sides of a triangle."). Two ideas and Learning words named the shape they showed, so the picture added nothing ("Does this one fit both ideas?"). Who has what asked about a ball, a hat, a cup, a spoon, a sock and a block it never drew (each now drawn, and "What does the cat have?" and "Who feels happy?" said once). Three steps every day cited VII.A.3 as if describing were all that waited (its next, before and after, and yesterday, today and tomorrow are now named), Things that happen's last line was a new "like a" list that grew the picture candidates (it now reads like the people half's, "like birthday party, rainy day and bedtime", and the tool skips the cue "like a happy cheer"), and five EARMARKS sentences named the old halves.
  - **Accuracy (6 to fix).** "Does snow fall on a rainy day? No" (rain and snow can fall together; the row became "Is a birthday party when you sleep in your bed?"); the picture and name kinds set rain against snow and a book against a birthday party, which the tap kind already barred (PE_EVENT_NOT now bars them too); "What is the opposite of day?" with Cold and Hot heard "Cold is the opposite of hot." and was left with one choice in 20 percent of seeds (the wrong words now come from two other pairs); "It fits only one idea" heard "but it fits none" while the answer was open (now "would mean it is a square, or it is blue."); "Playing together is more fun with a plan." told as fact in four places (now "can be"); and "saying them does" help four-year-olds remember (now "can", as the evidence for five-year-olds and the pre-K 3 row say). Taken from its suggestions too: "A baby is very little, and can drink milk from a bottle." (not every baby drinks from one), "Saying them can help you remember them all." in Three steps, the birthday song before the candles, and the match meaning "like a cup that matches a cup".
  - **Stories (story check 11 to fix; flow check 8).** The block house and Clothes in the basket taught their other halves' lessons at their turns (they now end on building together and on "Cat, duck and hat. Which one does not go with the others?"); Bodhi never put the little plate back, Mika never put her cups down, the bunny was fed without coming back, Two baskets quoted the old direction, Lior's third "is it bedtime?" and Yael's whisper had no voice of their own, and Remi shared a name with Remy, Yara's brother (now Rowan). Looks that repeated another character in the course were rewritten (Bodhi, Zane and his mom, Ivo's grandma, Lior and his grandma, Lulu, Rowan, the pizza shop's teacher, Mika's dad and the farmer, who had no hair written). The flow check's "Remember, ... like, get a cup" openers now say "like this.", the doubled opener in Things that happen is gone, "Two socks that are just alike match." reads "When two socks are just alike, they match.", grandma is cheered rather than squeaky, and the pre-K 4 voices no longer repeat pre-K 3's for count, match and corner. A title that ends in a question mark is now asked as a question (storyTitleSpoken), where "Is it bedtime yet?." had been read as a statement in sixteen titles.
  - **The 2027 standards (6 to fix).** PK3 VII.B.3 (see the lessons), PK4 I.B.2.c's new "with decreasing adult assistance" now cited in part in Feelings and what we do and Taking turns, PK3 II.A.1 read as pre-K 4 reads it, I.C.1 taught between Please and thank you's words and Talking with a friend's nonverbal skills, PK3 I.A.1's personal boundaries cited in Talking with a friend (both with plan rows), and EARMARKS L17 and A9 and RULES-AUDIT section 10 say what pass MR adopted. (27 pixels left at 390) takes the same three columns, and Wonder Questions and Progress by course hang their ⓘ beside the words, so the words alone are centered; tests/e2e/layout-check.mjs now reads words set straight in a centered row (a text node, which it had missed), proven on a planted row (15 pixels off) and a hung one (none).
